slides.headline: She multiplied two 13-digit numbers in 28 seconds. No calculator, no paper.
Shakuntala Devi, the 'Human Computer,' was born November 4, 1929, in Bangalore.
slides.body: In June 1980, Imperial College London's Computer Department verified her multiplying two randomly generated 13-digit numbers correctly in 28 seconds - a feat that entered the 1982 Guinness Book of World Records.

slides.headline: Her mental arithmetic feats made her a global phenomenon decades before anyone talked about Indian talent in STEM.
slides.body: Google marked her 84th birth anniversary with a Doodle in 2013 - recognition that outlasted her lifetime and crossed into how the world remembers Indian mathematical talent.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still runs on the same raw mathematical talent Devi showed the world decades ago.
slides.body: Her career is a reminder that India's claim to mathematical excellence isn't a recent story - it's one the world has been watching for generations.
